title: ACES standardized configurable cyber-range specification coverage protocol
claim: ACES provides a portable, typed scenario, experiment, and apparatus specification surface for the preregistered representative cyber-agent evaluation requirements without requiring backend deployment vocabulary in core SDL.
research_question: Can the preregistered atomic concepts be expressed, validated, instantiated, and compiled at their owning ACES stages without silent semantic loss or backend lock-in?

classification_rules.directly-expressible: A named typed ACES SDL or portable experiment field owns the meaning and every applicable production stage preserves it at an exact pointer.
classification_rules.profile-or-manifest-constraint: A named versioned profile, manifest, apparatus constraint, or realization envelope owns the constraint and validates independently from core SDL.
classification_rules.deliberately-backend-specific: The concept is a realization mechanism rather than portable scenario meaning and remains in a backend-facing disclosure or apparatus record.
classification_rules.missing: No existing typed owning surface preserves the requested meaning; prose, arbitrary metadata, and approximations do not count.

artifact_stages.canonical_entrypoint: backend-facing realization or apparatus disclosure; not core SDL

sources.title: A Survey of Cyber Range Training Exercise Scenario Description, Generation, and Execution
CybORG: A Gym for the Development of Autonomous Cyber Agents
Automating the Generation of Cyber Range Virtual Scenarios with VSDL

requests.title: Describe and validate a representative multi-host evaluation range
requests.paraphrase: Author topology, participant roles, objectives, workflows, evidence expectations, and apparatus requirements as distinct typed concerns.

requests.title: Describe an autonomous cyber-agent evaluation environment
requests.paraphrase: Declare participant identity, actions, observations, outcome measures, and the tools or affordances available to the participant.

requests.title: Specify constrained configurable virtual infrastructure
requests.paraphrase: Declare resource-constrained topology, test constraint satisfiability, and keep provider-specific image and deployment mechanics out of portable scenario meaning.

requests.title: Bind simulation apparatus and exchange cyber events
requests.paraphrase: Declare the execution clock/apparatus context separately from a typed federated cyber object and event exchange surface.

carriers.description: Authored participant, evidence, objective, and workflow scenario meaning.
Authored multi-host topology, constraints, objectives, and workflow meaning.
Published experiment task and apparatus constraint contract.
Published apparatus identity, clock, and measurement context contract.
Backend-facing profile and realization disclosure outside core SDL.
No current typed participant tool or affordance carrier.
No current typed federation object and event exchange carrier.

concepts.title: Multi-host network topology
concepts.meaning: Named hosts, networks, links, and dependencies form the evaluation environment.
concepts.success_rule: Every topology element is typed and survives at an exact compiled address.
concepts.fail_rule: Topology requires provider vocabulary or disappears before compilation.

concepts.title: Exercise participant roles
concepts.meaning: Red, blue, and evaluator responsibilities remain scenario roles rather than control-plane identities.
concepts.success_rule: A typed entity role survives compilation without becoming an authentication identity.
concepts.fail_rule: The role is prose-only or conflated with backend authorization.

concepts.title: Evaluation objectives
concepts.meaning: Actors, targets, windows, and success conditions are declared independently from scored measures.
concepts.success_rule: The objective and its success bindings survive at exact authored and compiled pointers.
concepts.fail_rule: Success meaning is free-form or dropped by the compiler.

concepts.title: Portable control workflow
concepts.meaning: Objective ordering, branching, retry, and terminal control remain backend-neutral.
concepts.success_rule: The workflow validates and compiles to a typed control graph.
concepts.fail_rule: The workflow depends on backend commands or loses control edges.

concepts.title: Authored evidence expectations
concepts.meaning: Portable capture obligations remain distinct from captured evidence and derived measures.
concepts.success_rule: A typed evidence requirement survives admission at an exact pointer.
concepts.fail_rule: Evidence intent exists only as notes or is mistaken for proof of capture.

concepts.title: Processor and backend selection constraints
concepts.meaning: Experiment apparatus choices are typed and version-bound outside core SDL.
concepts.success_rule: The published experiment task contract validates named processor/backend constraints.
concepts.fail_rule: Apparatus choice leaks into SDL or remains an unvalidated note.

concepts.title: Autonomous participant identity and scope
concepts.meaning: A participant has typed identity, initial knowledge, actions, observation boundary, and operating scope.
concepts.success_rule: Participant meaning validates and survives at an exact compiled agent address.
concepts.fail_rule: The participant is only a backend process or loses its information boundary.

concepts.title: Participant action contract
concepts.meaning: Action preconditions, effects, evidence expectations, and failure classes are declared independently from backend commands.
concepts.success_rule: The action contract survives compilation at an exact canonical address.
concepts.fail_rule: Action meaning requires a backend command or is silently weakened.

concepts.title: Participant observation boundary
concepts.meaning: Participant-visible, hidden, and evidence-only information are declared separately from world truth.
concepts.success_rule: The observation boundary survives compilation at an exact canonical address.
concepts.fail_rule: World truth and participant-visible state collapse or require backend interpretation.

concepts.title: Outcome measure
concepts.meaning: A benchmark metric names its construct, unit, direction, and evidence requirements outside SDL objectives.
concepts.success_rule: The published experiment task validates a typed metric definition.
concepts.fail_rule: A reward label or objective prose is treated as a measure.

concepts.title: Participant tool and affordance declaration
concepts.meaning: The authored task declares which bounded tools and decision affordances are available to the participant.
concepts.success_rule: A typed portable carrier owns tool and affordance availability.
concepts.fail_rule: Availability is only backend policy, prose, or arbitrary metadata.

concepts.title: Resource-constrained virtual topology
concepts.meaning: Virtual nodes carry typed CPU, memory, network, and dependency constraints without provider resource names.
concepts.success_rule: Typed portable resource constraints survive compilation.
concepts.fail_rule: Constraints require OpenStack, Docker, or cloud-provider fields.

concepts.title: Solver-backed constraint satisfiability
concepts.meaning: The authored infrastructure constraints can be checked for global satisfiability before realization.
concepts.success_rule: A typed formal constraint surface and solver result own the claim.
concepts.fail_rule: Local validation is presented as global satisfiability.

concepts.title: Provider-specific image and provisioning mechanics
concepts.meaning: Provider image, Terraform, and Packer choices are realization mechanics rather than portable SDL meaning.
concepts.success_rule: Provider mechanics remain in a backend-facing disclosure outside core SDL.
concepts.fail_rule: Provider vocabulary becomes a required SDL structural field.

concepts.title: Execution clock context
concepts.meaning: Clock authority, time domain, and synchronization are recorded as apparatus context.
concepts.success_rule: The published apparatus context validates a typed clock record.
concepts.fail_rule: Clock context is inferred from mutable runtime state.

concepts.title: Federated cyber object and event exchange
concepts.meaning: A portable typed contract exchanges cyber objects and events across independently implemented simulation federates.
concepts.success_rule: A published portable exchange contract preserves object/event identity and provenance.
concepts.fail_rule: Exchange depends on backend-private payloads or has no typed carrier.

objective_pass_criteria: Every load-bearing concept is directly expressible or profile/manifest constrained, every declared stage passes at an exact pointer, backend-specific mechanics remain outside core SDL, and no requested meaning is silently lost.
objective_fail_criteria: Any load-bearing concept is missing, invalid, silently weakened, or requires backend vocabulary in core SDL; or an applicable production stage fails while the analysis claims success.
validity_threats: The four sources and sixteen atomic concepts are representative but do not exhaust cyber-range or cyber-agent evaluation requirements.
Repository-owned examples test the pinned reference implementation and do not prove independent backend conformance.
Source requests are bounded paraphrases of cited records; no paper or standard bytes are copied into the bundle.
Results apply only to the pinned ACES revision and named production entrypoints.
A missing supplemental concept keeps the broad claim partial even when every issue-defined load-bearing concept passes.
